verdict.rationale: Sentry's own self-hosting docs say it makes its source code publicly available, and users report reading that code to build advanced integrations, so the source can be read. Community reports of the BSL relicensing, with some users now calling it closed-source, mean the license is source-available rather than clearly open, so the 'open license' half of the story is only partly met. Missing for 10: a documented OSI-approved open license for the core product, first-party documentation of the license terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: In addition to making its source code available publicly, Sentry offers and maintains a minimal setup that works out-of-the-box for simple use cases.
the fully open source code helped a ton with advanced integrations, since they could see exactly what happens instead of relying only on the docs
Despite the BSL change they will keep using Sentry and remain customers.
